learning: Iteration 2 gave s-bend progress of 0.04 with zero line loss, against 0.1475 at iteration 1 (12 mm array, kp 4.0). The drop may come from the kp change, from the 16 mm footprint, or from both, so this race holds the geometry fixed to separate them. If the s-bend still drifts with no line loss, test a larger ki (for example 0.2) to remove a steady motor-mismatch offset before changing the geometry again.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's iteration 3 geometry, which is identical to iteration 2 (16 mm contiguous sensors at ±0.048 m). Only kp is held at 5.0 from iteration 2; the other controller values are unchanged, so the race isolates gain on the same sensing.
rationale: Iteration 2 (16 mm contiguous sensors at x = ±0.048 m, kp 5.0) removed line loss on the oval and s-bend (0 events on both) but did not produce completions. The s-bend ended off track at max_error 0.0611 m with progress only 0.04, and the slalom still shows one line-loss event per run with max_error 0.0628 m. The remaining failure is drift or turn-rate lag, not a detection gap. The Builder's proposal keeps the iteration 2 geometry, so this race isolates controller gain on the same sensing. I therefore keep kp 5.0 as the only controller setting that differs from iteration 1. I keep the weights proportional to x (-1.0 to +1.0) so a positive signal steers left, as the contract requires. I leave ki at 0.05, kd at 0.3, base_speed at 1.5 and line_loss at last_direction, because no evidence yet shows they limit the result. ki is the next candidate if the s-bend shows a steady one-sided drift, since a fixed motor mismatch produces a constant offset that a larger integral term would remove. I expect line_loss_events to stay at 0 on the oval and s-bend, max_error to stay below about 0.061 m, and s-bend progress to rise above the iteration 2 value of 0.04. I cannot verify this before the race.
